input:
A shell-and-tube exchanger heats crude oil in a refinery preheat train at a duty of 954 kW. The hot stream enters at 95 °C and leaves at 70 °C; the cold stream enters at 25 °C and leaves at 40 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger is 49.8 K and the installed area is 66.9 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 286 W m-2 K-1. The coefficient is a derived figure, computed as the duty divided by the product of the installed area and the log-mean temperature difference, on the values stated above.

Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The figures therefore describe the exchanger in its assessed state, under the conditions of the run from which the fouling assessment comes. Each stream temperature is a terminal value for the exchanger as a whole; no distribution of temperature through the passes is reported, and none is implied by the figures above. A cleaned exchanger would return a different coefficient, and the present figures cannot say by how much, because the comparison they rest on has not been run.

The duty is heat passed from the hot stream to the cold stream inside the one exchanger, and the exchanger is reported as a single item of equipment.
